messages:
liam: Hey all, first week q about secrets: my service needs to call a partner API and the partner handed us a long-lived API key. What's the recommended path for onboarding that key and any immediate rotation/escrow steps? Also curious about emergency oncall access to secrets.
jessica: Welcome @liam! Short answer: store the partner key in Vault as an external/static secret with a rotation plan, but prefer to wrap it with envelope encryption via our KMS if it's used server-side. File the request using the onboarding form (https://redwood-internal/new-hire-secrets) and tag it "third-party" + env.
ryan: For service identities, create a dedicated service account (prod/regulatory: <proj>-svc-prod, dev: <proj>-svc-dev). Use Vault AppRole or IAM auth depending on runtime. If running on k8s, prefer Kubernetes auth with projected service account tokens.
liam: For rotation: partner can't automate rotations. Do we rotate ourselves, and how do we signal downtime to the partner?
secops: If partner doesn't support rotation, we rotate on our side by creating a new key in Vault and updating consumers behind a canary rollout. Document the change window for the partner and use a short-lived proxy token if possible. We require a rotation cadence in the request: 30d prod minimum for high-risk keys, 90d default for standard vendor keys.
jessica: Add an approver who knows the partner integration (owner + security). For any key used in client-side apps (browsers/mobile) we block it and ask for strict token exchange patterns.
liam: Emergency oncall: how does SRE/dev oncall get short-term access if something breaks in production?
platform-team: We use the emergency access flow in the secrets runbook. Oncall can request a break-glass short-lived token via the ops portal; it creates a temporary Vault role with 1h TTL and audit logging. Must get a one-time approval from secops.
ryan: Also, add a note in your request if you want an "oncall-access" tag so reviewers can pre-authorize a runbook-based escalation.
liam: Any examples for the form body?
jessica: Example you can paste: 
"Service: payments-ingest
Environment: prod
Secrets: partner-foo-api-key
Access pattern: backend service only, Vault AppRole (k8s->AppRole bridge)
Rotation: manual rotate by owners every 30d; notify partner 72h before swap
Approvers: payments-engineering lead, secops"
devex-bot: Secrets request queued: SR-2026-342. Assigned to secops-review. Tracker: https://redwood-internal/requests/SR-2026-342
secops: FYI: if you need CMK/envelope encryption, include usage (at-rest vs envelope) and regulatory flag. CMKs are scoped to prod and require extra compliance review (can add 2-3 business days).
liam: For local dev, what's simplest? Put a dev key in Vault and use the dev vault-agent?
platform-team: Yes, use dev Vault instances or Vault Agent with a dev role. If you do persist a dev key locally, put it in OS keychain and mark it dev-only. Never commit in plaintext.
liam: Thanks everyone, filing the request now and adding the oncall tag. Appreciate the quick responses :pray:
